scope: Full read-only review of manuscript, appendices, generated examples/tables/plots, bibliography, and all 19 rendered PDF pages. No manuscript or code edits.
overall_verdict: Revise before release. The artifact account is technically careful and the plots are useful, but the stated AI-assisted case-study contribution needs a more concrete evidence-backed development narrative. Several bounded presentation corrections will improve the fit to the intended community-request story.

assessments.narrative: The title, opening paragraph, and request citation align the paper with a documented community need. The central AI-development account is currently much thinner than the tactic and compilation account.
assessments.mathematics: The finite characterization and appendix distinguish abstraction completeness from bounded program behavior and handle equality differences, zero costs, and strict comparisons. No mathematical defect was identified in this editorial reading; this is not an independent formal verification.
assessments.experiments: The paper carefully distinguishes selected replacements from unattended discoveries, proof savings from infrastructure cost, and workload timing from algorithm speed. It retains slower files and explains conditional block assumptions. No new timing experiment is needed for the scoped claims.
assessments.plots: Both panels match the stated 582 original lines, 226 replacement lines plus 46 imports, and 46 file ratios including seven slower files. The total interval is separated from the file distribution. Legends and marks remain legible in the PDF.
assessments.examples: Checked averaging, quantified, metric, reverse-triangle, unsupported-product, and operator examples provide useful scope coverage. The exact motivating request is discussed but its Lean invocation is not shown in the paper.
assessments.citations: The request is supported by the primary Zulip archive, the HOL Light source supports NORM_ARITH, and the Solovay-Arthan-Harrison arXiv record supports the general decidability claim. The immutable Isabelle URL could not be fetched in this review; no conclusion about its availability or correctness is drawn.
assessments.layout: All 19 pages were visually inspected. No missing glyphs, overlaps, clipped text, or unreadable plots were found. Page 4 has substantial spare space. Census floats interrupt the timing methods across pages 11-14.

findings.title: Make the AI-development contribution concrete enough to evaluate
findings.finding: The declared contribution is a case study in AI-assisted development, but the development section names the tools and describes module boundaries; Appendix D mainly repeats attribution and limitations. It does not yet tell the reader what the agents actually produced at successive stages, what was checked before accepting their work, or one concrete failure/correction that the validation caught. A commit trailer establishes attribution, not a development method.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact evidence-backed sequence from the ChatGPT starter to the recorded Codex expansion and library-patch validation, with artifact/commit references. Include one concrete documented correction or rejected approach if the repository supports it. State human steering or review roles only where recorded; explicitly leave unrecorded effort unknown. Explain the practical lesson that AI-generated reusable tooling can be accepted through proof and source checks. Page 4 has room, so the central account need not be hidden behind the long evaluation appendix.

findings.title: Distinguish the implemented request fragment from the broader dream tactic
findings.finding: The cited conversation begins with the exact displayed norm inequality, but later expands the request to normed-algebra reasoning involving products of norms. The manuscript correctly excludes products, yet the abstract says the tactic addresses this request without naming the narrower scope.
findings.recommendation: Describe the contribution as addressing the decomposition-search or vector-space part of the request. Add one short sentence acknowledging that the later normed-algebra/product extension remains outside the core. Keep the existing distinction between a documented request and community acceptance.

findings.title: Close the motivating request with a visible checked tactic call
findings.finding: The paper opens with the community inequality but immediately demonstrates a different averaging example. Appendix D only says that the same requested inequality occurs in the test module. A reader never sees the literal transition from community problem to tactic invocation in the paper.
findings.recommendation: Print a short checked Lean example for the exact requested inequality in the main text or as the first checked appendix example, with its source provenance. Retain the averaging example as evidence that rational search goes beyond the motivating case, if space permits.

findings.title: Label the 310-line quantity as savings
findings.finding: Table 1 labels the value 310 as "Net proof lines after helpers and imports". That reads as the remaining code count, but remaining replacement code plus imports is 272; 310 is the amount saved.
findings.recommendation: Change the generator label to "Net lines saved after helpers and imports" (or equivalent) and regenerate. Keep the underlying number unchanged.

findings.title: Define each file point as a ratio of paired-pass means
findings.finding: The caption says that each point represents a file and that ratios above one favor the replacement, but only the total statistic is explicitly defined in the main timing prose. It is not explicit whether file points are means of ratios, ratios of means, or individual-pass values.
findings.recommendation: Say each point is the ratio of mean original to mean replacement time across the 40 paired passes for that file. Retain the existing warning that the total interval concerns repeated workload timings and not variation across files.

findings.title: Keep census tables with the census explanation
findings.finding: Seven census/selection/cost tables float into the confirmatory-timing subsection. In the PDF, the bootstrap paragraph begins on page 11, resumes below census tables on page 12, and continues below more census tables on page 13. This makes it hard to distinguish the historical census from the measured timing protocol.
findings.recommendation: Flush the census tables after generated/census-detail.tex and before the historical-format and confirmatory-timing paragraphs, or give census and timing their own clear appendix subsections with float barriers.

findings.title: Report performed methods rather than protocol commands
findings.finding: The methods alternate between factual description and instructions such as "Count nonblank", "The census must include", and "Assign explicit classes". This leaves the reader uncertain whether those are executed procedures, intended requirements, or advice for a future replication.
findings.recommendation: Convert verified performed procedures to descriptive past/present tense and label any remaining protocol requirement explicitly. For example, say that the accounting counted preparation and that the extractor waited for finalized elaboration data if the artifacts establish those facts.

review_limits: No rerun of Lean proofs or experimental measurements by this reviewer.
No complete prompt transcript or human-effort record exists in the inspected evidence, so a causal AI-productivity claim is not supported.
